source.name: usp_GetTopCustomers
source.sourceDefinition:
CREATE   PROCEDURE dbo.usp_GetTopCustomers
    @TopN INT
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;
    SELECT TOP (@TopN)
        c.CustomerID,
        c.FirstName + ' ' + c.LastName AS FullName,
        COUNT(o.OrderID) AS OrderCount,
        ISNULL(SUM(o.TotalAmount), 0) AS TotalSpent,
        DATEDIFF(DAY, MAX(o.OrderDate), GETDATE()) AS DaysSinceLastOrder
    FROM dbo.Customers c
    LEFT JOIN dbo.Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
    GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.FirstName, c.LastName
    ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC;
END;

result.generatedDdl:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION dbo.usp_GetTopCustomers(
    p_TopN INT
)
RETURNS TABLE (
    CustomerID INT,
    FullName TEXT,
    OrderCount BIGINT,
    TotalSpent NUMERIC,
    DaysSinceLastOrder INT
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT 
        c.CustomerID,
        c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS FullName,
        COUNT(o.OrderID) AS OrderCount,
        COALESCE(SUM(o.TotalAmount), 0) AS TotalSpent,
        EXTRACT(DAY FROM (CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - MAX(o.OrderDate)))::INT AS DaysSinceLastOrder
    FROM dbo.Customers c
    LEFT JOIN dbo.Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
    GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.FirstName, c.LastName
    ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC
    LIMIT p_TopN;
END;
$$;
assumptions: The dbo schema exists in PostgreSQL or will be created
CustomerID column is of type INT in both Customers and Orders tables
FirstName and LastName are text-compatible types (VARCHAR, TEXT, etc.)
TotalAmount is a numeric type (NUMERIC, DECIMAL, or similar)
OrderDate is a DATE or TIMESTAMP type
The procedure returns a result set, so it's converted to a FUNCTION returning TABLE
SET NOCOUNT ON has no direct equivalent in PostgreSQL and is omitted (PostgreSQL doesn't send row count messages by default)
Parameter renamed from @TopN to p_TopN following PostgreSQL naming conventions

reviewFlags.reason: Verify the actual data type of CustomerID in the Customers and Orders tables. It might be BIGINT, SERIAL, or another integer type.
Verify the actual data type and precision of TotalAmount in the Orders table. May need to specify NUMERIC(precision, scale) for exact compatibility.

The DATEDIFF conversion assumes OrderDate is a DATE or TIMESTAMP. If it's a different type, casting may be required. Also, this calculation may produce different results if OrderDate includes time components.
Ensure that p_TopN is always a positive integer. Consider adding validation if NULL or negative values should be handled differently.

compatibilityNotes.description: SQL Server procedure returns an implicit result set; PostgreSQL function must be called with SELECT * FROM or used in a FROM clause.
SQL Server uses + for string concatenation; PostgreSQL uses ||. NULL handling differs: SQL Server returns NULL if any operand is NULL, PostgreSQL's || also returns NULL, so behavior is consistent.
DATEDIFF(DAY, ...) in SQL Server vs EXTRACT(DAY FROM interval) in PostgreSQL may produce slightly different results depending on time components and timezone handling.
SQL Server's TOP is converted to PostgreSQL's LIMIT. Both work similarly but LIMIT is applied after ORDER BY, which matches the SQL Server behavior in this case.
COUNT() returns BIGINT in PostgreSQL vs INT in SQL Server. This may affect client applications expecting specific integer sizes.
